items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: The name 'Barky' appears only in a parenthetical note '[(note)] x Barky 6. 1902, so 39 in 41.' The interviewee does not mention this person in their spoken narrative.

ctx.x: And if you remember, Nelson Rockefeller was in charge of Latin affairs at that time, and so we went around and we all did this together, Kirby and everybody, and we pulled all sorts of strings to get out of the country, down on this job. Because we had it all figured out. We could go down there, and I think it was a year, like we'd all go down there and continue exactly what we were doing and come back rich. Not rich, but well on our way, because you know, we were young at that time and you know, most of the…

But I don't know whether they thought that we just wanted to leave the country because of the war, on account of the war, you know. But the more we pursued, you know, what we wanted to do, it seemed the deeper the hole we were digging. Then the word got around to all the draft boards and everybody, about who's this bunch of people who want to -- you know, collectively. So it never came off. And that was the first inkling or the first happening that started the band on a downgrade, because Billy left, and the war…
